source.title: Honda–Tate theory for Shimura varieties
source.authors: Mark Kisin, Keerthi Madapusi Pera, Sug Woo Shin
source.version: 41-page author PDF, creation metadata 2021-01-27. Author publication lists associate it with Duke 2022; final published text not compared.
readSections: All 41 pages freshly read contiguously, including Appendix A and references; image checks at PDF pages 6,11,14,19,20,26,28,29,34,37.

summary: Kisin, Madapusi Pera and Shin show that the Newton strata of a Shimura variety of Hodge type are non-empty when the group G is quasi-split at p, confirming a conjecture of Fargues and Rapoport in that case, without assuming a good integral model (G may be ramified at p). They conjecture that every mod p isogeny class contains the reduction of a special point, a refinement of Honda–Tate theory, and prove a large part of this for PEL type, through Tate's theorem with additional structures, independence of ℓ and CM lifts. Reviewed by REV-PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 244 items (16 library, 38 planned, 190 missing). 48 mistakes are confirmed (32 misprints, 5 gaps, 11 errors; 5 reach a stated result, 8 a proof); E10 is rejected as not a mistake. Theorem 3 and Corollaries 1.3.16 and 1.3.18 need the μ-ordinary class, which exists when G is quasi-split at p (E8), and Corollary 1.3.18 also needs the hypotheses of [KP18] (E27). Lemma 2.3.13 is false as stated, but the lift built in Proposition 2.3.11 satisfies the missing condition, so Corollaries 2.3.14 and 2.3.15 stand (E41). Theorems 1, 2 and 4–6 stand. Not formalised.

structure DividedPowers where
  /-- The divided power function underlying a divided power structure -/
  dpow : ℕ → A → A
  dpow_null : ∀ {n x} (_ : x ∉ I), dpow n x = 0
  dpow_zero : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 0 x = 1
  dpow_one : ∀ {x} (_ : x ∈ I), dpow 1 x = x
  dpow_mem : ∀ {n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I), dpow n x ∈ I
  dpow_add : ∀ {n} {x y} (_ : x ∈ I) (_ : y ∈ I),
    dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y
  dpow_mul : ∀ {n} {a : A} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x
  mul_dpow : ∀ {m n} {x} (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m x * dpow n x = choose (m + n) m * dpow (m + n) x
  dpow_comp : ∀ {m n x} (_ : n ≠ 0) (_ : x ∈ I),
    dpow m (dpow n x) = uniformBell m n * dpow (m * n) x

def reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ObjectProperty (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k) :=
  geometricNormalSubgroupFreeCommHopfAlgProperty k
    (smoothUnipotentCommHopfAlgProperty (AlgebraicClosure k))

declarations.statementRead:
theorem reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty_iff (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (H : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, u} k) :
    reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty k H ↔
      Algebra.Smooth k H ∧
        geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty k H.obj ∧
          ∀ I : HopfIdeal (AlgebraicClosure k)
              (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := AlgebraicClosure k) H),
            I.IsNormal →
              geometricallyConnectedCommHopfAlgProperty (AlgebraicClosure k)
                (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.quotient
                  (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.baseChange (K := AlgebraicClosure k) H) I).obj →
              smoothUnipotentCommHopfAlgProperty (AlgebraicClosure k)

qualifications: WittVector.isocrystal_classification assumes finrank exactly one; it does not supply Dieudonne-Manin in all ranks.
The reductive-group and torus predicates are built. Their rational Newton, sigma-conjugacy, local-global cohomology and Shimura interfaces are separate contracts.

The dominant-chamber uniqueness result is for a finite reduced crystallographic root system with the flipped pairing reduced and strictly ordered coefficients. The central torus and rational coroot cone adapters were N05, removed on review as not in the paper.
TauCeti.posRootCone in RootSystem/Positive.lean uses integral nonnegative coefficients. It does not by itself supply the rational dominance cone used here.
The abelian-variety and finite-surjective isogeny carriers are reused; the relative universal family, rational Hom tensor functor and isogeny torsors are additional contracts.
A divided-power structure is not a PD envelope, log site, convergent isocrystal or crystalline comparison theorem.
Proposed API wrappers on library items are not additional claims that their names or full contracts are implemented.

items.name: Geometric isogeny
items.statement: (§2.3.1) For s0, s0' ∈ S_{K_p}(F̄_p), Hom_Q(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) is the scheme over Q assigning to a Q-algebra R the group R ⊗ Hom(A_{s0},A_{s0'}), the Hom-space taken in the prime-to-p isogeny category. For a Q-algebra R, an R-isogeny from A_{s0} to A_{s0'} is an element f ∈ Hom_Q(A_{s0},A_{s0'})(R) for which there exists f' ∈ Hom_Q(A_{s0'},A_{s0})(R) with f'∘f ∈ Aut_Q(A_{s0})(R).

items.name: Absolute Hodge tensor realizations
items.statement: Fix tensors {s_α} ⊂ V^⊗ (V^⊗ = ⊕_{m,n≥0} V^{⊗n}⊗V^{*⊗m}) whose pointwise stabilizer in GL(V) is G. There are global sections {s_α,dR} ⊂ H^0(Sh_K, V_dR^⊗) and {s_α,ét} ⊂ H^0(Sh_K, V_ét^⊗) (V_ét = V^p × V_p, the duals of the prime-to-p and p-adic Tate modules of A) such that (1.3.4.1) for κ algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and s ∈ Sh_K(κ) there is an isomorphism V_{A_f} ≅ H^1_ét(A_s, A_f) = V_ét,s, determined up to G(A_f), carrying {s_α} to {s_α,ét,s}; (1.3.4.2) writing s_α,p for the projection of s_α,ét onto V_p, for every finite extension L'/L and s ∈ Sh_K(L') the de Rham comparison (1.3.3.3) carries {1⊗s_α,p,s} to {1⊗s_α,dR,s}. Construction: [Kis10, (2.2)], resting on Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties over C are absolutely Hodge; (1.3.4.2) is attributed to Blasius–Wintenberger [Bla94].

items.name: Abelian Serre-Tate deformation
items.statement: (As used in the proof of Prop. 1.3.7, p.17.) items.name: Algebraic fundamental group
items.statement: For a connected reductive group G over a field F and a maximal torus T ⊂ G, the algebraic fundamental group π1(G) [Bor98] is a Gal(F̄/F)-module, functorial in G, canonically isomorphic to X_*(T)/X_*(T^sc). items.name: Unramified replacement preserving Galois averages
items.statement: Let H_0 be an absolutely simple quasi-split adjoint group over a finite extension F/Q_p, with a Borel subgroup B_0 ⊂ H_0 and a maximal torus T_0 ⊂ B_0 over F. Let (H,B,T) = Res_{F/Q_p}(H_0,B_0,T_0), X = X_*(T), C ⊂ X_Q the Γ_p-invariant positive chamber determined by B, and N: C → C the Galois averaging map (§1.1.9). Let F'/Q_p be the unramified extension with [F':Q_p] = [F:Q_p]. Then there is a quasi-split absolutely simple adjoint group H'_0 over F', with a Borel subgroup B'_0 and a maximal torus T'_0 ⊂ B'_0, such that: (1.1.10.1) with (H',B',T') = Res_{F'/Q_p}(H'_0,B'_0,T'_0), there is an isomorphism of triples (H,B,T)⊗_{Q_p}Q̄_p ≅ (H',B',T')⊗_{Q_p}Q̄_p; (1.1.10.2) with C' ⊂ X'_Q the positive chamber of X' = X_*(T') determined by B' and N': C' → C' its Galois averaging map, the isomorphism in (1.1.10.1) can be chosen so that the induced isomorphism C' ≅ C carries N' to N. The proof, though not the printed statement, also makes H'_0 split over an unramified extension of F', so that H' is unramified. Proposition 1.1.13 uses the lemma in that form. The isomorphism matches the averaging maps, not the Galois actions.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure. Correction: in the statement H′_0 must split over an unramified extension of F′, so that H′ is unramified (E14).
proofSteps: Reduce to absolutely simple adjoint factors and their diagram actions. Replace the extension by an unramified one of equal degree. Only averaging operators must agree; use N25 for the exceptional noncyclic triality action.

items.name: General rational-Levi minuscule lift (corrected: absolute Weyl group)
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over Q_p, M ⊂ G a Q_p-rational Levi subgroup, T ⊂ M a maximal torus, μ ∈ X_*(T) a cocharacter that is minuscule as a cocharacter of G, and [b_M] ∈ B(M)_b such that ([b_M],{μ}) is G-admissible. Then there is w in the absolute Weyl group W(G,T) such that ([b_M],{w·μ}) is M-admissible. Equivalently, some G(Q̄_p)-conjugate μ' of μ factoring through M makes ([b_M],{μ'}) M-admissible. The printed conclusion, w ∈ W(G,M) := N_G(M)/M, is false (errata E2).
items.note: Corrected formulation and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026), following the structure of the paper's proof with the correct Weyl group. The only use, Corollary 1.1.17 (N32), needs exactly this: its proof writes "By Lemma 1.1.13, there exists w∈W(G,T)". The remaining inputs are N27 and its cited unramified result, and Kottwitz97 4.4, under G-local. The G-source gate for the normalizer statement is resolved by this correction. Correction: the proof must take P* and its Levi factor M* both Q_p-rational (E18).
proofSteps: Choose a rational parabolic P with Levi M and an inner twisting ξ:G→G* to the quasi-split form with ξ(P)=P* rational, as in the paper. Then ξ|_M:M→M* is an inner twisting, and B(M)_b≅π₁(M)_Γ=π₁(M*)_Γ≅B(M*)_b gives [b_{M*}].

Let μ* be the B*∩M*-dominant representative of ξ|_M∘μ. The pair ([b_{M*}],{μ*}) is G*-admissible. The κ-condition holds by functoriality of the Kottwitz maps and the compatible identifications π₁(M)=π₁(M*), π₁(G)=π₁(G*). The Newton condition holds because the Newton points of basic classes lie in X_*(A_{M*})_Q and are determined by κ ([Kot97, 4.4]). This is the paper's own argument.
Apply N27 (Proposition 1.1.13) to G*: there is w* in W(G*,T*), not only in N_{G*}(M*)/M*, with ([b_{M*}],{w*·μ*}) M*-admissible. The paper's proof misquotes this output as w*∈W(G*,M*).

Transport back along ξ, which identifies W(G,T)(Q̄_p) with W(G*,T*) after conjugating ξ(T) to T* inside M*. For basic b_M, M-admissibility of ([b_M],{μ′}) is the κ_M-equality κ_M(b_M)=μ′^♯ in π₁(M)_Γ (Lemma 1.1.6), which transports through π₁(M)=π₁(M*).

items.name: Local-global torus cohomology obstruction sequence
items.statement: Let T be a torus over Q. For each place v of Q (including v = ∞, with Γ_∞ = Gal(C/R)) there is a canonical isomorphism j_v: H^1(Q_v,T) ≅ X_*(T)^{tors}_{Γ_v} [Kot86, (1.1.1)]. items.name: Weil number and Weil point
items.statement: Let l be a prime (possibly equal to p). An element α ∈ Q̄ is an l-Weil number of weight w ∈ Z if α is an l-unit and all its complex embeddings have absolute value l^{w/2}. Let H be an algebraic group over Q. An element γ ∈ H(Q) is an l-Weil point if, for some faithful representation W of H (defined over any field of characteristic 0), the eigenvalues of γ on W are l-Weil numbers (not necessarily of a common weight). γ ∈ H(Q) is a Weil point if it is an l-Weil point for some l.

items.name: Extension over a mixed-characteristic DVR
items.statement: Lemma 1.3.6. Let S = Spec R with R a discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), generic point η, and s: η → 𝒮_K. The following are equivalent: (i) s extends to S → 𝒮_K; (ii) A_η has good reduction; (iii) A_η has potentially good reduction. [Implicit hypothesis needed for (ii)⇒(i): R is an O_E,(v)-algebra compatibly with s, i.e. the valuation of R restricts to v on E; see E22.] Proof: (i) ⇔ s extends to S → S_𝒦 (normality of 𝒮_K), so (i) ⇔ (ii) ⇒ (iii); for (iii) ⇒ (i) extend over a finite flat R'/R and descend since R' ∩ Frac R = R.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.
proofSteps: Potential good reduction makes the inertia action finite; the rigidifying level forces the relevant finite action to be trivial. Apply Neron-Ogg-Shafarevich and the ambient Siegel extension, then use normalization to lift. Preserve the precise level hypotheses from Lemma 1.3.6.

There is a closed immersion Û^an → Û^an_{L'} of smooth irreducible rigid spaces over L', and Û^an_{L'} is an open ball. items.statement: Proposition 1.3.10. Let ι_p: Q̄ ↪ Q̄_p be chosen so that E ↪ Q̄_p induces v (standing assumption stated just before Lemma 1.3.9, p.18). Assume hypothesis (1.1.3.1) for G_Qp and [b] ∈ B(G_Qp). Then ([b], {μ_X^{-1}}_p) is admissible if and only if there exists s0 ∈ 𝒮_K(F̄_p) with [b] = [b_s0].

Let 𝒮_0 be the normalization of Spec O_{E_T,(v')} in Sh_0. items.name: Tensor functor for the universal crystalline realization
items.statement: The realization V to D extends to an exact faithful tensor functor Rep_Qp(G) to F-Isoc of the geometric special fiber. Prove tensor generation and descent; do not identify the monodromy subgroup with all of G solely because selected tensors are preserved.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.
proofSteps: Let H=Aut^⊗(ω_s) for the full tensor subcategory generated by D, where ω_s forgets Frobenius after evaluation and scalar extension. Global chosen tensors imply H⊂G_s, not H=G_s. Use restriction Rep_L(G_s)→Rep_L(H), together with the G_s-torsor Isom_sα(V_L,D_s), to construct the functor after scalar extension.

To descend to Q_p, enlarge the tensor family by each G-invariant morphism between finite sums of mixed tensors. Its étale realization must be a global absolute-Hodge section; apply S10/A16 and A18 to extend it and detect identity, composition, tensor, dual and idempotent relations. This enlargement and the original absolute-Hodge input remain G-tensors.

Use tensor generation of finite-dimensional Rep(G) by a faithful V and char-zero reductive semisimplicity: every representation is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of mixed tensors. Split the transported idempotents in F-Isoc, descend morphisms through these summands, and verify independence of presentation and exact faithfulness with pointwise fiber functors. Retain G-tensors until these categorical and source inputs are supplied. Do not assert the displayed equivalence with all of Rep_L(G_s).

items.name: Density under local integrality

Local integrality and the source connectedness result force irreducibility of the corresponding special fibers. Use isogeny/Hecke correspondences with their changing levels to transfer nonemptiness; an open nonempty subset of each component is dense.

items.name: Tame special-parahoric density specialization
items.statement: Printed Corollary 1.3.18: 'Suppose that p > 2, and that G splits over a tamely ramified extension, and K_p is a special parahoric. Then the embedding G ↪ G_V can be chosen such that S_[b_μ] is dense in 𝒮_{K,k(v)}.' Proof: Cor. 1.3.16 and [KP18, Cor. 0.3]. Audit of KP18 (Publ. IHÉS 128 (2018), Introduction p.122–124): Cor. 0.3 is stated under the standing assumptions p > 2, (G,X) of abelian type, G_Qp tamely ramified, p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, K°_p parahoric, and gives a normal (hence locally integral) special fibre only 'If K°_p is associated to a point x which is a special vertex in B(G, Q_p^ur)'. Safe statement: p > 2, G_Qp tamely ramified, p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, K_p = K°_p the parahoric attached to a special vertex of B(G, Q_p^ur) (very special). Such a vertex forces G_Qp quasi-split, so [b_μ] exists and satisfies (1.1.3.1) (C02, N16); then for a suitable Hodge embedding the special fibre is locally integral and S17 gives density.

items.name: Accommodating symplectic embedding
items.statement: Let ι: (G,X) ↪ (G_V, H_V) be the given embedding. ι is strictly accommodating if (i) for some totally real field K, G^der = Res_{K/Q} G^s with G^s absolutely almost simple, and the G^der-representation V has the form Res_{K/Q} V^s for an admissible G^s-representation V^s; (ii) if (G^s, V^s) is of type D^R, then for every character χ: Z_G → G_m over Q̄, the χ-part of V is an admissible representation of a factor of G^der_{Q̄}; (iii) for every proper non-zero G-stable subspace V' ⊂ V, if G' denotes the image of G in Aut V', then (G', V') does not satisfy (i) and (ii). ι is accommodating if there are finitely many strictly accommodating embeddings ι_j: (G_j, X_j) ↪ (G_{V_j}, H_{V_j}), j = 1,…,s, and an isomorphism of symplectic spaces ∏_j V_j ≃ V inducing a commutative square (G,X) → (G_V,H_V), ∏_j (G_j,X_j) → (∏_j G_{V_j}, ∏_j H_{V_j}), such that the left vertical map induces G^der ≃ ∏_j G_j^der. (The paper prints 'accommodating' for 'strictly accommodating' in the second definition: E4.)

items.name: Accommodating-case character-polynomial argument
items.statement: Assume ι is accommodating and let γ ∈ I_{s0}(Q) be a neat l-Weil point. Let V ⊗ Q̄ = ⊕_{i=1}^n W_i be the decomposition of the G-representation V into isotypic components. The subalgebra Q̄^n ⊂ End_{Q̄} V_{Q̄} acting by scalars on each W_i descends to a product of fields L = ∏_{i=1}^k L_i ⊂ End_Q V, which gives a decomposition V = ∏_{i=1}^k V_i. Let P_{i,γ,ℓ} be the characteristic polynomial of γ acting (via i_ℓ) on V_{i,Q̄_ℓ}. Then P_{i,γ,ℓ} does not depend on ℓ (proof of [Noo06, 6.13]). Its roots are l-Weil numbers, no two of which differ by a non-trivial root of unity ('faiblement net', from neatness). By [Noo09, Lem. 2.5, 2.6] the image of i_ℓ(γ) in Conj'(G)(Q̄_ℓ) is independent of ℓ and lies in Conj'(G)(Q̄). This is Proposition 2.2.2 for accommodating ι; the paper says the proof is the same as that of [Noo09, Thm. 2.4].
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.
proofSteps: Decompose over a splitting field into isotypic summands whose scalar algebra descends. Compare each factor characteristic polynomial, use neatness to rule out nontrivial root-of-unity ratios, and invoke Noot reconstruction in each classical type.

items.name: Auxiliary accommodating Shimura correspondence
items.statement: (§2.2.7, p.27.) Lift s0 to s ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(Q̄_p); fixing Q̄_p ≃ C, s is the image of (h_0, 1) ∈ X × G(A_f). By [Del79b, 2.3.10] (see [Noo06, 2.12]) there is an accommodating embedding ι': (G',X') ↪ (G_{V'}, H_{V'}), with (V',ψ') a symplectic Q-space and a map G'^der → G^der inducing (G'^ad, X'^ad) ≃ (G^ad, X^ad). By real approximation for G^ad, after conjugating G'^der → G^der by an element of G^ad(Q), the image of X' in X^ad contains h_0. Let G'' be the identity component of G' ×_{G^ad} G, let X'' be the G''(R)-orbit of (h_0, h_0') ∈ X ×_{X^ad} X', where h_0' is the point of X' over h_0^ad, and let V'' = V ⊕ V' with ψ'' = ψ ⊕ ψ'; ι'': (G'',X'') → (G_{V''}, H_{V''}) is induced by ι and ι'. [As printed, G'' does not lie in G_{V''} = GSp(V'',ψ''); it must be cut down to the pairs with equal similitude factors (E32).] This gives maps S_K(G,X) ← S_{K''}(G'',X'') → S_{K'}(G',X'). s lifts to s'' ∈ S_{K''}(G'',X'')(Q̄_p); A_{s''} has good reduction (Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, as in [Noo09, p.68]), so by Lemma 1.3.6 s'' specializes to s0'' lifting s0. Let s0' be its image. Then there are maps A_{s0} ← A_{s0''} → A_{s0'}, corresponding to the projections of V'' onto V and V'. The two projectors are G''-invariant and are added to the Hodge cycles, so the surjections G'' → G, G'' → G' induce I_{s0} ← I_{s0''} → I_{s0'}. By Corollary 2.1.9 these are surjective and induce I_{s0}/Z_G ≃ I_{s0''}/Z_{G''} ≃ I_{s0'}/Z_{G'}.

items.name: Rational abelian-quotient map
items.statement: There is a Q-group map I_x→G_ab whose base change equals the maps induced by i_ℓ for every ℓ. The auxiliary Shimura datum must be G′=G×_{G^ab}T, pairs (g,t) with the same image in G^ab, not the printed G×T.
items.note: Repair and proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5, 22 September 2026). With the printed G′=G×T the construction fails twice: G×T is not in GSp(V⊕V,ψ⊕ψ), and the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} contains 1×T, which maps onto G^ab. This is recorded in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22.json (E5). The remaining inputs, Corollary 2.1.9 and Noot, stay under G-noot.
proofSteps: For a special point (T,h_T) of (G,X) put G′=G×_{G^ab}T⊂G×T acting on V′=V⊕V, with T acting on the second copy through T⊂G. Similitude factors through G^ab, so G′⊂GSp(V′,ψ⊕ψ). Since h^ab is constant on X, X′=X×{h_T} maps into Hom(S,G′_R), giving an embedding of Shimura data (G′,X′)↪(GSp(V′),H′).

As in the paper, conjugating T→G by G^ad(Q), the point s₀ lifts to s′₀ on the integral model for (G′,X′). A_{s′₀} is isogenous to A_{s₀}×A_T, and I_{s′₀} preserves the decomposition. Restriction to A_T gives I_{s′₀}→T; compose with T→G^ab.

Kernel check: the kernel of I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} (restriction to A_{s₀}) lies, after base change to any Q_ℓ, in ker(G′→G)={(1,t):t∈T∩G^der}. That kernel maps trivially to G^ab. So the composite kills ker(I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀}), and since I_{s′₀}→I_{s₀} is surjective (Corollary 2.1.9) it factors through a Q-map I_{s₀}→G^ab.

Compatibility with i_ℓ: over Q_ℓ, the map I_{s₀}→G^ab so obtained and the composite I_{s₀}⊗Q_ℓ≅I_{ℓ,s₀}→G_{Q_ℓ}→G^ab_{Q_ℓ} agree on the image of I_{s′₀}, because for (g,t)∈G′ the images of g and t in G^ab coincide.

items.statement: For abelian varieties over a finite field after sufficiently divisible finite extension, rational Hom tensor Q_ell equals Frobenius-equivariant Hom on Tate modules for ell distinct from p, and the contravariant crystalline counterpart for ell=p. Restrict to invertible maps to compare T26 with realization Isom schemes.

items.name: Tensor-preserving isogeny torsors
items.statement: For ℓ ≠ p, P_ℓ(s0,s0') ⊂ Isog_ℓ(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) is the closed subscheme of the isomorphisms (which already carry γ_{m,ℓ,s0} to γ_{m,ℓ,s0'}) that carry 1⊗s_{α,ℓ,s0} to 1⊗s_{α,ℓ,s0'} for each α. For ℓ = p, P_p(s0,s0') ⊂ Isog(D_{s0},D_{s0'}) is the closed subscheme of the φ-equivariant isomorphisms R⊗D_{s0'} → R⊗D_{s0} carrying 1⊗s_{α,cris,s0'} to 1⊗s_{α,cris,s0}. P(s0,s0') ⊂ Isog(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) is the largest closed subscheme defined over Q that maps into P_ℓ(s0,s0') for every ℓ, including ℓ = p. P(s0,s0') is either empty or an I_{s0}-torsor; P_ℓ(s0,s0') is an I_{ℓ,s0}-torsor when non-empty (proof of Lemma 2.3.5).

items.name: Uniqueness of special torus Frobenius up to finite order
items.statement: Two T(Q)-points satisfying the same p-unit and Kottwitz valuation conditions have a ratio of finite order. Use discreteness in finite adeles for this compact-mod-scalars torus and compactness of the local valuation kernel; do not assert finite-adelic discreteness for arbitrary Q-tori.

proofSteps: Take the ratio, whose kappa vanishes at p and whose other finite components are bounded. For this particular torus rational points are discrete in the finite adeles because of its compact real quotient modulo scalars; intersection with the compact local kernel is finite.

items.name: Conditional geometric CM lift
items.statement: If G is quasi-split at p, G_ad has no type-D factor and TT holds for all point pairs, every x and maximal T in I_x admit a Qbar-isogeny CM lift with respect to T. The construction must use the inverse Hodge cocharacter consistently.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.
proofSteps: Transfer T rationally, choose a cocharacter in it whose average is the Newton cocharacter, and construct a special pair. Its reduction has the same torus Frobenius after a power by T34,T44,T35. Local tensor torsors are nonempty, and the explicit TT hypothesis supplies the geometric global torsor.

items.name: Torus reduction of the isogeny torsor
items.statement: As printed: suppose s0 ∈ S_{K_p}(F̄_p), T ⊂ I_{s0} a maximal torus, and s0 admits a Q̄-isogeny CM lift (j,x,s0') with respect to T. Let P^T = P^T(s0,s0') ⊂ P(s0,s0') be the subscheme of isomorphisms that respect the action of T. Then P^T is a T-torsor whose class in H^1(Q_v,G) is trivial for every place v of Q ('of G' misprinted). As printed this is false in general. It needs the extra hypothesis γ_{m,s0} = γ_{m,s0'} in T(Q) for m sufficiently divisible (T acting on A_{s0'} through j, §2.3.9), which the lift built in the proof of Proposition 2.3.11 satisfies. The proof also shows that the class of P^T in H^1(R,T) is trivial, and Corollary 2.3.14 uses this.
items.note: A source-based extraction target with the stated gates. This checkpoint does not certify recursive closure.
proofSteps: At infinity use the polarization-torsor comparison. Away from p, full prime-to-p level gives a trivial G-torsor. At p write the two Frobenii in T and compare their integral kappa values; the torsor cocycle has trivial image in H1(Q_p,G).

items.name: Torus Newton invariant is the Galois average
items.statement: For an F=Q_p torus T and λ∈X_*(T), let [b_T]=κ_T^{-1}([λ]). Then ν_T(b_T)=N_Γ λ in X_*(T)_Q^Γ. The average is rational; κ_T still retains integral coinvariant torsion.
proofSteps: Use the natural isomorphism X_*(T)_Γ→B(T) normalized by valuation one on G_m (Kottwitz85 §§2.2–2.5). For a finite Galois splitting field E/F and maximal unramified subfield E_0, a representative is N_{E/E_0}(λ(π_E))∈T(E_0)⊂T(L). The alternative finite splitting extension over L used by KMPS has the same normalization.

Pair with every F-rational character χ. The representative has valuation ⟨χ,λ⟩; the invariant rational cocharacter is uniquely determined by these pairings. Equivalently, Kottwitz85 (2.8.1) is precisely finite orbit averaging.

Kottwitz85 §4.4 identifies this valuation map with the tensorial Newton map. Thus the Newton formula follows without discarding κ torsion. The sign-action lattice has nonzero Z/2 coinvariant but zero rational average.
items.note: Explicit continuation proof/adapter; no Lean implementation claimed. Original dependencies retain their gates.

items.name: Ordinary class for a quasi-split group
items.statement: For connected reductive G/Q_p quasi-split, any geometric cocharacter class {μ} has a unique [b_μ]∈B(G,{μ}) with ν=μ^diamond. Choose a Q_p-rational Borel pair T⊂B and B-dominant μ∈X_*(T). The image of κ_T^{-1}([μ]) has the required invariants. A rational Newton representative exists. This algebraic existence statement does not by itself prove density in an integral model.
proofSteps: Choose the rational Borel pair supplied by quasi-split reductive-group theory, with T a maximal torus. The Galois action preserves the dominant chamber; averaging its finite orbit gives a dominant invariant rational cocharacter μ^diamond.
Send the torus class κ_T^{-1}([μ]) into B(G). Functoriality gives κ_G=μ^sharp and ν_G equal to the dominant orbit of N_Γ μ=μ^diamond. Hence it is admissible and attains the Hodge bound.

All other admissible classes have the same κ and smaller or equal ν. Equality gives equality of classes by N11. N16, with Kottwitz85 Proposition 6.2, supplies (1.1.3.1). The rational Borel-pair and general classification prerequisites are still part of G-local.
items.note: Kept as the corrected form of the existence assertion of §1.3.15 (E8), which holds for quasi-split G_{Q_p}. Kottwitz (1985), §§2.8, 4.4 and 6.2, supplies the torus average and the rational Newton representative; Kisin–Zhou (arXiv:2103.09945v2, Remark 2.2.5) records the same restriction.

items.name: Derived subgroup, simply connected cover, T^sc
items.statement: For a connected reductive group G over a field F, G^der ⊂ G is its derived subgroup and G^sc → G^der is the simply connected cover of G^der. For a maximal torus T ⊂ G, T^sc is the preimage of T in G^sc, a maximal torus of G^sc.

items.name: Absolute Weyl group W(G,T) with Galois action
items.statement: For a maximal torus T of a connected reductive group G over F, W(G,T) = N_G(T)(F̄)/T(F̄) is the absolute Weyl group. It acts on X_*(T), and Gal(F̄/F) acts on W(G,T) with γ(w·x) = γ(w)·γ(x). So Gal(F̄/F) acts on X_*(T)_Q/W(G,T).
items.locator: Notational conventions, p.5; used in §1.1.1, p.5
items.note: Needed for N(G) = (X_*(T)_Q/W(G,T))^{Γp} (N03) to make sense. Planned: the Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap, Layer 7, plans the Weyl group and the absolute root datum with its Galois action.

items.name: Fixed closures, embeddings and Galois groups
items.statement: For each place v of Q fix an algebraic closure Q̄_v (Q_∞ = R, Q̄_∞ = C). Fix Q̄ and embeddings ι_v: Q̄ ↪ Q̄_v for every v. Set Γ_v = Gal(Q̄_v/Q_v) and Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q), and view Γ_v ⊂ Γ via ι_v. In §1.1, Γ_p = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p).
items.note: Every Γ_p-(co)invariant in §1.1 depends on these choices. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: L̄, the embedding Q̄_p ↪ L̄, and Q_{p^r}
items.statement: With L = W(F̄_p)[1/p], fix an algebraic closure L̄ of L and an embedding Q̄_p ↪ L̄. Cocharacters defined over L, such as ν_b, are regarded as G(Q̄_p)-classes through this embedding. Q_{p^r} denotes the fixed field of σ^r on L, that is W(F_{p^r})[1/p].
items.note: The paper uses this to view ν̄_G([b]) as a point of N(G) and in (1.1.2.2)/(1.1.4.1). L01/L02 cover only W, L and σ. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Map δ_G: N(G) → (π1(G)⊗Q)^{Γp}
items.statement: There is a unique map N(G) → π1(G)^{Γp} ⊗ Q = (π1(G)⊗Q)^{Γp} that is functorial in G and is the identity N(T) = X_*(T)_Q^{Γp} = (π1(T)⊗Q)^{Γp} when G = T is a torus. It is induced by the W(G,T)-invariant projection X_*(T)_Q → X_*(T)_Q/X_*(T^sc)_Q = π1(G)⊗Q.
items.note: Checked in RR96 (numdam copy), pp.161–162: Theorem 1.15(iii) gives the unique natural transformation that is the natural identification for tori. N10 uses this map but no item defines it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Averaging isomorphism (π1(G)⊗Q)_{Γp} ≅ (π1(G)⊗Q)^{Γp}
items.statement: Let M be a finitely generated Γ_p-module on which Γ_p acts through a finite quotient Q. Then [x] ↦ |Q|^{-1} Σ_{γ∈Q} γx (the average over the Γ_p-orbit) is an isomorphism (M⊗Q)_{Γp} → (M⊗Q)^{Γp}. For M = π1(G), composed with π1(G)_{Γp} → (π1(G)⊗Q)_{Γp}, this is the right vertical arrow of (1.1.2.1).
items.note: N10 needs it. The same averaging defines Nμ* in §1.1.5 and N in §1.1.9. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Conjugation isomorphism int(g): J_b ≅ J_{b'}
items.statement: If b' = g b σ(g)^{-1} with g ∈ G(L), then h ↦ g h g^{-1} is an isomorphism of Q_p-groups int(g): J_b → J_{b'}.
items.note: Checked: from hb = bσ(h) it follows that (ghg^{-1})b' = b'σ(ghg^{-1}). This makes J_b depend only on [b] up to isomorphism, as §1.1.16 and Corollary 1.1.17 need. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Quasi-split inner form G*, inner twisting ξ, and (B*, T*, C̄*)
items.statement: For G connected reductive over Q_p, G* is the quasi-split inner form of G over Q_p and ξ: G_{Q̄p} → G*_{Q̄p} is an inner twisting: an isomorphism with ξ^{-1}∘γ(ξ) inner for every γ ∈ Γ_p. B* ⊂ G* is a Borel subgroup over Q_p, T* ⊂ B* a maximal torus over Q_p, and C̄* ⊂ X_*(T*)_R the closed B*-dominant chamber. If G is quasi-split, take G* = G and ξ = id.
items.note: Existence and uniqueness of the quasi-split inner form is a black box. N19/N20 use this setup, but no item states it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Transfer N_ξ: N(G) → N(G*)
items.statement: If the G(Q̄_p)-conjugacy class of ν: D_{Q̄p} → G_{Q̄p} is defined over Q_p, then so is the G*(Q̄_p)-conjugacy class of ξ∘ν. This defines N_ξ: N(G) → N(G*), which depends only on the G*(Q̄_p)-conjugacy class of ξ. If G is quasi-split and ξ = id, N_ξ is the identity.
items.note: Condition (1.1.5.2) uses it. Checked: γ(ξ∘ν) = γ(ξ)∘γ(ν) = Int(g_γ)∘ξ∘γ(ν), which is conjugate to ξ∘ν. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: μ♯ and the identification π1(G)_{Γp} = π1(G*)_{Γp}
items.statement: For a G(Q̄_p)-conjugacy class {μ} of cocharacters G_{m,Q̄p} → G_{Q̄p}, μ♯ ∈ π1(G)_{Γp} is the image of {μ}; it is well defined because X_*(T) → π1(G) is W-invariant. The inner twisting ξ induces a canonical Γ_p-equivariant isomorphism π1(G) ≅ π1(G*) that does not depend on ξ [RR96, 1.13]. Under π1(G)_{Γp} = π1(G*)_{Γp} the image of μ* is μ♯.
items.note: Condition (1.1.5.1), Lemma 1.1.6 and Lemma 1.1.8 use it. The symbol on the page is ♯ (sharp), as the items write. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: N_ξ is compatible with the maps to π1 ⊗ Q
items.statement: The maps N(G) → (π1(G)⊗Q)^{Γp} and N(G*) → (π1(G*)⊗Q)^{Γp} are intertwined by N_ξ and the canonical isomorphism π1(G) ≅ π1(G*). In particular N_ξ sends a central class to the central class of G* with the same image in π1⊗Q.
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Lemma 1.1.6, p.8
items.note: The paper never states this. Lemma 1.1.6 needs it for non-quasi-split G to compare N_ξ(ν̄_G([b_bas(μ)])) with μ̄*. It holds on X_*(T)_Q level because ξ induces the W-equivariant isomorphism that defines π1(G) ≅ π1(G*). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Elliptic maximal torus
items.statement: A maximal torus T' ⊂ G over Q_p is elliptic if T'/Z(G) is anisotropic over Q_p, equivalently X_*(T')_Q^{Γp} = X_*(Z(G))_Q^{Γp}.
items.note: Lemma 1.1.8 and later results use this notion (Proposition 1.2.5 via tori elliptic at p) without defining it. Kot85's proof of 5.3 uses the form X_*(T)^Γ ⊂ X_*(Z). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: [Kot85, Prop. 5.3]: B(T) → B(G) has image B(G)_b for elliptic T
items.statement: Let T ⊂ G be an elliptic maximal Q_p-torus. Then the image of B(T) → B(G) equals B(G)_b.
items.note: A cited black box; checked on Kot85 p.215. Lemma 1.1.8 uses only image ⊂ B(G)_b: the Newton point of b ∈ T(L) lies in X_*(T)^Γ_Q ⊂ X_*(Z)_Q. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: [RR96, Prop. 2.4(ii)]: a basic class lies below every class with the same δ
items.statement: Let b̄, b̄' ∈ B(G) with δ(b̄) = δ(b̄') in π1(G)^Γ ⊗ Q. If b̄ is basic, then b̄ ⪯ b̄'. Lemma 1.1.6 needs the pointwise form: if ν̄, ν̄' ∈ N(G) have the same image in (π1(G)⊗Q)^{Γp} and ν̄ is central, then ν̄ ⪯ ν̄'. This holds because a dominant element of X_*(T^der)_Q is a nonnegative combination of simple coroots [Bou, VI §1.6].
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 1.1.6, p.8; [RR96, Prop. 2.4(ii)], p.166
items.note: A cited black box; checked on RR96 p.166, where it is stated for elements of B(G). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Quasi-split groups: ν_b has a G(L)-conjugate defined over Q_p
items.statement: If G is quasi-split over Q_p and b ∈ G(L), there is g ∈ G(L) with Int(g)∘ν_b defined over Q_p. Hence b' = gbσ(g)^{-1} satisfies (1.1.3.1).
items.locator: §1.1.3, p.7; [Kot85, proof of Prop. 6.2, p.219] (a variant of Kottwitz 1984 Lemma 1.1.3)
items.note: This black box justifies the first case of N16. It uses σ-stability of the G(L)-class of ν_b ([Kot85, (4.4.3)]). Checked on Kot85 p.219. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Admissibility for tori reduces to κ
items.statement: Let T be a torus over Q_p, so that T* = T, ξ = id, and ⪯ is equality on N(T). For μ ∈ X_*(T), the pair ([b], μ) is admissible iff κ_T([b]) is the image of μ in X_*(T)_{Γp}, iff [b] = [b_bas(μ)] = κ_T^{-1}([μ]). The Newton condition ν̄_T([b]) = Nμ then follows automatically from (1.1.2.1).
items.locator: Implicit in Definition 1.1.7 and Lemma 1.1.8, p.8; used in the proof of Proposition 1.3.10, p.18
items.note: Lemma 1.1.8 concludes 'T'-special' without checking that ([b_bas(μ')], μ') is T'-admissible; this fact, or Lemma 1.1.6 applied to G = T', supplies it. Proposition 1.3.10 also uses it: 'admissible for T_{Q_p}. But then we must have [b_{s0}] = [b]'. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Conjecture 1 (statement only)
items.statement: Suppose G_{Q_p} is quasi-split. Then for every x ∈ S(F̄_p), the isogeny class of x contains the reduction of a special point. Isogenies here are isogenies A_x → A_{x'} carrying s_{α,x} to s_{α,x'} in ℓ-adic cohomology for every ℓ ≠ p and in crystalline cohomology.
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as a hypothesis like T29/T45. Theorem 5 refers to it ('so that Conjecture 1 holds in this case', p.4). Conjecture 2.3.8 (T45) is a refinement. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Galois averaging on the chamber of a Weil-restricted absolutely simple adjoint group
items.statement: Let H_0 be an absolutely simple quasi-split adjoint group over a finite extension F/Q_p, with a Borel subgroup B_0 and a maximal torus T_0 ⊂ B_0 over F. Set H = Res_{F/Q_p}H_0, B = Res B_0, T = Res T_0 and X = X_*(T), a free Z-module with Γ_p-action. B gives a Γ_p-invariant positive chamber C ⊂ X_Q, and the Galois averaging N: C → C (Nx = [Γ_p:Γ_x]^{-1} Σ_{γ∈Γ_p/Γ_x} γx, as in §1.1.5) has image in C^{Γ_p}. Explicitly, the Dynkin diagram of H is ⊔_{σ:F→Q̄_p} D_0, where D_0 is that of H_0. The stabilizer Γ_σ of σ (the pointwise stabilizer of σ(F)) acts on D_0 by ρ_σ, with ρ_σ(γ) = ρ_{σ_0}(τ^{-1}γτ) when τ∘σ_0 = σ. The simple coroots are the α^∨(σ,d_0), for σ an embedding and d_0 a vertex. If d_{0,1},…,d_{0,r} is the Γ_σ-orbit of d_0, then Nα^∨(σ,d_0) = (r[F:Q_p])^{-1} Σ_{σ', 1≤i≤r} α^∨(σ',d_{0,i}).
items.locator: §1.1.9, p.8; explicit formula in the proof of Lemma 1.1.10, p.9
items.note: The input to Lemma 1.1.10 (N24, N25). The formula depends only on [F:Q_p] and on the orbits of ρ_{σ_0}(Γ_{σ_0}) on D_0; this is the key to the proof. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Standard Levi subgroup of a quasi-split group
items.statement: Let G be quasi-split over Q_p, B ⊂ G a Borel subgroup over Q_p and T ⊂ B a maximal torus over Q_p. A standard Levi subgroup M ⊂ G is the centralizer of a split torus T_1 ⊂ T. The group X_*(Z_M)^{Γ_p}_Q is regarded as a subset of N(M).
items.note: Used in N26–N28 and in the proofs of Corollaries 1.1.15 and 1.1.17. The paper's definition is broader than 'Levi factor of a parabolic containing B' (e.g. in GL_3 the centralizer of diag(a,b,a)). Every such M is G(Q_p)-conjugate, by an element of N_G(T), to a B-standard one, so nothing depends on the difference. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Central cocharacter ν_{b,J} of J_b
items.statement: Let G be possibly non-quasi-split and b ∈ G(L), with hypothesis (1.1.3.1) for G and [b]. Via the inner twisting J_b ≅ M_[b] of §1.1.4, the Q_p-rational central cocharacter ν_G([b]) of M_[b] induces a central cocharacter ν_{b,J}: D → J_b defined over Q_p. If b is replaced by a σ-conjugate satisfying (1.1.4.1), then J_{b,L} = M_{ν_b} and the inner twisting is this identification followed by int(h), for some h ∈ G(L) carrying ν_b to ν_G([b]). Then ν_G([b]) = int(h)(ν_{b,J}) as G-valued cocharacters.
items.locator: §1.1.16, p.12; the description via h is in the proof of Corollary 1.1.17, p.13
items.note: Appears in the conclusion of Corollary 1.1.17 (N32), ν_{b,J} = Nμ_{T'}. No item defines it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Wintenberger: admissible classes meet the Cartan double coset (unramified G)
items.statement: Let G be unramified over Q_p, with a reductive model over Z_p (again denoted G) in which T extends to a maximal torus over W, and let μ ∈ X_*(T) be minuscule. If b ∈ G(L) and ([b],{μ}) is admissible, then there is g ∈ G(L) with g^{-1}bσ(g) ∈ G(W)μ(p)G(W).
items.note: Black box, applied to b = b_M. The unramified case of Proposition 1.1.13 starts from it. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Reduction of the Cartan double coset to a Levi (Iwasawa and Satake)
items.statement: Let G be as in the previous item, M ⊃ T a standard Levi (it extends to a Levi subgroup over W), and N the unipotent radical of a parabolic with Levi factor M. (a) Iwasawa: G(L) = N(L)M(L)G(W). (b) [LR87, Lem. 5.2]: if b_M ∈ M(L), m ∈ M(L), n ∈ N(L) and (nm)^{-1}b_Mσ(nm) ∈ G(W)μ(p)G(W), then m^{-1}b_Mσ(m) ∈ M(W)μ'(p)M(W) for some μ' ∈ X_*(T) with μ' ≼_G μ and with the same image as μ in π_1(G). (c) If μ is minuscule, μ' is W(G,T)-conjugate to μ (cf. [Kot03, Thm. 1.1, 4.1], [Kis17, (2.2.2)]).
items.note: Black box, only sketched in the paper. The paper states only μ' ≼_G μ in (b); the π_1 condition is needed for (c) (see E16). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Mazur's inequality for unramified groups [RR96, Thm. 4.2]
items.statement: Let M be an unramified reductive group over Q_p, with a reductive model over W containing the maximal torus T, and let μ' ∈ X_*(T). If x ∈ M(W)μ'(p)M(W), then ([x],{μ'}) is M-admissible: κ_M([x]) = μ'^♯ and ν̄_M([x]) ≼_M μ̄'.
items.note: Black box. Rapoport–Richartz give the Newton inequality; the κ part holds because κ is trivial on M(W). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Rational parabolics and Levi factors in a quasi-split group
items.statement: Let G* be quasi-split over Q_p. Every G*(Q̄_p)-conjugacy class of parabolic subgroups that is defined over Q_p contains a Q_p-rational parabolic subgroup P*. P* has a Q_p-rational Levi factor, and any two Levi factors of P* are R_u(P*)(Q̄_p)-conjugate.
items.note: Standard (Borel–Tits). The first clause is used as printed; the second is needed to make M* = ξ(M) rational (see E18). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Basic classes of inner-twisted Levi subgroups: Kottwitz and Newton compatibility
items.statement: Let ξ: G → G* be an inner twisting with ξ(P) = P* and ξ(M) = M* Q_p-rational, so that ξ|_M: M → M* is an inner twisting. (a) [RR96, 1.13]: there are canonical isomorphisms π_1(M)_{Γ_p} = π_1(M*)_{Γ_p} and π_1(G)_{Γ_p} = π_1(G*)_{Γ_p}, compatible with the Levi embeddings. Hence B(M)_b ≅ π_1(M)_{Γ_p} = π_1(M*)_{Γ_p} ≅ B(M*)_b via κ_M and κ_{M*}. (b) [Kot97, 4.4]: N_{ξ|_M}∘ν̄_M on B(M)_b and ν̄_{M*} on B(M*)_b factor through X_*(A_{M*})_Q ⊂ N(M*), where A_{M*} is the maximal split central torus of M*, and are determined by κ via X_*(A_{M*})_Q ≅ π_1(M*)_{Γ_p}⊗Q. So corresponding basic classes satisfy N_{ξ|_M}(ν̄_M([b_M])) = ν̄_{M*}([b_{M*}]), and hence N_ξ(ν̄_G([b_M])) = ν̄_{G*}([b_{M*}]).
items.note: The black boxes that transport the admissibility of ([b_M],{μ}) to G*. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Basic Levi representative of [b] attached to a transferred torus
items.statement: Assume (1.1.3.1), and take b satisfying (1.1.4.1), with the inner twisting J_b ≅ M_[b] given by int(h) as above. Let T' ⊂ J_b be a maximal torus with a transfer j: T' → M_[b]. Let T_1 ⊂ j(T') be the maximal split subtorus and M = Cent_G(T_1), so that j(T') is an elliptic maximal torus of M. Let m ∈ M_[b](L) satisfy m j_0 m^{-1} = j, where j_0: T' → J_b ≅ M_[b]. Then b_M := mh·b·σ(mh)^{-1} commutes with j(T'(Q_p)) and lies in M(L), and ν_{b_M} = ν_G([b]) is central in M. So [b_M] ∈ B(M)_b and it maps to [b] ∈ B(G). After replacing the fixed maximal torus T of G by one containing a maximal split torus T_2 ⊃ T_1, M ⊃ T is a standard Levi.
items.note: This construction reduces Corollary 1.1.17 to Corollary 1.1.15 (corrected) and Lemma 1.1.8. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Existence of elliptic maximal tori
items.statement: Every connected reductive group over Q_p (here J_b) contains an elliptic maximal torus defined over Q_p. By [Kot86, §10] such a torus transfers to M_[b].
items.note: Standard black box. It is needed to apply Corollary 1.1.17 when G_{Q_p} is not quasi-split. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Tori through h_y are anisotropic modulo the centre
items.statement: Let (G,X) be a Shimura datum, y ∈ X, and T_∞ ⊂ G_R a maximal torus through which h_y factors. Then the preimage T_∞^{sc} of T_∞ in G^{sc}_R (equivalently, the image of T_∞ in G^{ad}_R) is anisotropic over R, because int h_y(i) is a Cartan involution of G^{ad}_R, so the centralizer of h_y in G^{ad}_R is compact. Consequently every ω ∈ W(G,T)(C) commutes with complex conjugation on T^{sc}, for T any maximal torus whose T_R is G(R)-conjugate to T_∞.
items.note: Asserted without proof ("Since T^sc is anisotropic over R"); it follows from Deligne's axiom SV2. It is the hypothesis of item G07. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Twisting a global maximal torus by a class that dies in G^sc
items.statement: Let T ⊂ G be a maximal torus over Q and α ∈ H^1(Q,T^{sc}) with trivial image in H^1(Q,G^{sc}). Then there is g ∈ G^{sc}(Q̄) with gσ(g)^{-1} ∈ T^{sc}(Q̄) for all σ ∈ Γ, such that α is represented by σ ↦ gσ(g)^{-1}, and int(g^{-1})(T_{Q̄}) is a maximal torus of G defined over Q. (i) If α_p = 0, then g = s·g_p with s ∈ T^{sc}(Q̄_p) and g_p ∈ G^{sc}(Q_p). So int(g^{-1})|_T = int(g_p^{-1})|_T is induced by G(Q_p)-conjugation, which preserves the image in B(G_{Q_p}) of [b_bas(μ^{-1})] for μ ∈ X_*(T). (ii) Suppose α_∞ is the class of n n̄^{-1}, with n ∈ N_{G^{sc}}(T^{sc})(C) over ω, and gḡ^{-1} = t n n̄^{-1} t̄^{-1} with t ∈ T^{sc}(C). Then h = g^{-1}tn ∈ G^{sc}(R), and int(h) agrees with int(g^{-1})∘ω on X_*(T).
items.note: The core of the proof of Proposition 1.2.5. Part (i) is used only implicitly in the last sentence ("the pair (T,μ_x) satisfies the conclusions of the proposition"). Items G05, G07 and G22 supply its inputs. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 1.1.14: [RV14, Lem. 8.2(ii)] for quasi-split groups
items.statement: Proposition 1.1.13 confirms that part (ii) of [RV14, Lem. 8.2] holds for all quasi-split G (cf. [RV14, Rem. 8.3]). There [b_M] is not assumed basic in B(M); one reduces to the basic case by [Kot85, Prop. 6.2].
items.note: A numbered remark, not used later. Include only if remarks are extracted. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Hodge-type Shimura variety embeds in the Siegel one at suitable level (cited)
items.statement: Let (G,X) ↪ (G_V, H_V) be a Hodge embedding, V_(p) ⊂ V a Z_(p)-lattice on which ψ is Z_(p)-valued, and K_p ⊂ G(Q_p), 𝒦_p ⊂ G_V(Q_p) the stabilizers of V_p = Z_p ⊗ V_(p). For every sufficiently small compact open K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p) there is a neat compact open 𝒦^p ⊂ G_V(A_f^p) such that, with K = K_pK^p and 𝒦 = 𝒦_p𝒦^p, the map Sh_K(G,X) → Sh_𝒦(G_V,H_V) ⊗ E is a closed immersion.
items.note: Used in the proof of Prop. 1.3.7 ('This map is a closed immersion, since the map Sh_K → Sh_𝒦 is') and in §2.1.1 ('an embedding on generic fibres'). P03 does not state it. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Deligne: Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolutely Hodge (cited)
items.statement: Every Hodge cycle on an abelian variety over C is absolutely Hodge.
items.note: Black-box input for the existence of the global sections s_α,dR, s_α,ét and property (1.3.4.1). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B1 plans the absolute-Hodge statements for the realizations of Hodge tensors in Hodge type.

items.name: Blasius–Wintenberger: absolute Hodge cycles are compatible with the p-adic de Rham comparison (cited)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A with an absolute Hodge cycle t, over a p-adic field K' of the kind considered, the de Rham comparison B_dR ⊗_{Q_p} H^1_ét(A_{K̄'}, Q_p)^⊗ ≅ B_dR ⊗_{K'} H^1_dR(A/K')^⊗ carries 1 ⊗ t_p (the p-adic étale component) to 1 ⊗ t_dR.
items.note: The paper applies it to points over finite extensions L'/L with L = W(F̄_p)[1/p]; [Bla94] is stated for abelian varieties over number fields, so the scope extension (presumably via [Kis10, (2.2)]) should be recorded with the item. Not flagged as a mistake. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Berthelot rigid generic fibre of normal complete local formal schemes (cited)
items.statement: For the formal schemes in the proof of Prop. 1.3.7 (formal completions at a closed point of normal flat finite-type O_{L'}-schemes, and the formally smooth 𝒰̂_{L'}), Berthelot's rigid generic fibre is functorial, takes the finite map Û → 𝒰̂_{L'} to a map of rigid spaces over L', takes normal complete local domains to irreducible (connected, normal) rigid spaces, and takes Spf of a formally smooth complete local O_{L'}-algebra to an open polydisc.
items.note: Used to make Û^an → 𝒰̂^an_{L'} a map of smooth irreducible rigid spaces and 𝒰̂^an_{L'} an open ball. The exact wording should be taken from de Jong, Publ. IHÉS 82 (1995), §7.3. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Category F-Isoc(S) of F-isocrystals
items.statement: For a scheme S of characteristic p, F-Isoc(S) is the isogeny category obtained by localizing the category of F-crystals on S (crystalline site of S over Z_p) [RR96, §3]. It is a Q_p-linear (non-neutral) Tannakian category whose unit object 1 is the structure sheaf of the crystalline site.
items.note: End(1) = Q_p needs S connected; the proof of Cor. 1.3.13 accordingly works on connected components. S09 presupposes this category but no item defines it. Missing: routed to route 4.

items.name: Universal F-isocrystal 𝒟 on the geometric special fibre
items.statement: The crystalline realization (rational contravariant Dieudonné crystal) of the universal abelian scheme A over 𝒮_K is an object 𝒟 ∈ F-Isoc(𝒮_K ⊗_{O_E,(v)} F̄_p) whose restriction to each s0 ∈ 𝒮_K(F̄_p) is the F-isocrystal D_s0.
items.note: Used in Prop. 1.3.12 (S10), Cor. 1.3.13 (S11) and Thm. 1.3.14. P06 covers only the pointwise D_s0. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Tannakian subcategory C_𝒟, its L-linear extension, and its group
items.statement: For a connected component S of 𝒮_K ⊗ F̄_p, C_𝒟 is the smallest full Tannakian subcategory of F-Isoc(S) containing 𝒟; C_𝒟,L = C_𝒟 ⊗ L is obtained by tensoring Hom-sets with L and adjoining direct summands for idempotents [Del79a, 2.1]. For s0 ∈ S(F̄_p), pull-back to s0 followed by forgetting Frobenius is an L-linear fibre functor ω_s0: C_𝒟,L → Vec_L with ω_s0(𝒟) = D_s0, so C_𝒟,L ≃ Rep_L(H), H = Aut^⊗(ω_s0). Because the s_α,cris,s0 are values of global morphisms 1 → 𝒟^⊗ (Prop. 1.3.12), H ⊂ G_s0 = Aut_{s_α,cris,s0}(D_s0). The paper asserts H = G_s0, which fails in general (E9).
items.note: S11 states only the corollary. The construction is where the E9 error sits. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Grothendieck–Katz specialization of Newton polygons (cited)
items.statement: Let S be a scheme of characteristic p and M an F-crystal on S. For every polygon P, the set of points of S at which the Newton polygon of M lies on or above P is Zariski closed.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.3.14, p.20, citing [Kat79, Thm. 2.3.1]
items.note: The proof also uses [RR96, Lem. 2.2(iv)] to reduce ⪯ on N(G) to GL_n, following [RR96, Thm. 3.6]. S12 cites only RR96 Thm 3.6. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Finiteness of B(G,{μ})
items.statement: For a connected reductive G over Q_p and a conjugacy class {μ}, the set B(G,{μ}) of classes [b] with ([b],{μ}) admissible is finite.
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of (1.3.14.2) and in §1.3.15, p.20
items.note: Local closedness of S_[b] from (1.3.14.1) and openness of the μ-ordinary stratum need the complement to be a finite union of the closed sets of (1.3.14.1), and κ constant on 𝒮_K by Lemma 1.3.9. S13 alludes to a 'finite dominance interval' without an item. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Connected components of 𝒮_K have irreducible special fibre under local integrality (cited)
items.statement: If the special fibre 𝒮_{K,k(v)} is locally integral, then every connected component of 𝒮_K has irreducible special fibre.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 1.3.16, p.20, citing [MP19, Cor. 4.1.11]
items.note: This is only the form used; MP19 was not available to check the exact statement. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Kisin–Pappas: reducedness/normality of the special fibre at parahoric level (cited)
items.statement: Assume p > 2, (G,X) of abelian type, G_Qp splits over a tamely ramified extension, p ∤ |π_1(G^der)|, and K°_p a parahoric subgroup, with the KP18 integral model S_{K°}(G,X) (for Hodge type, the normalization of the closure for a suitably chosen Hodge embedding). Then S_{K°}(G,X) ⊗ κ(v) is reduced, and the strict henselizations of its local rings have irreducible components that are normal and Cohen–Macaulay. If K°_p is associated to a point x that is a special vertex of B(G, Q_p^ur), then S_{K°}(G,X) ⊗ κ(v) is normal and Cohen–Macaulay.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 1.3.18, p.20, citing [KP18, Cor. 0.3] (Publ. Math. IHÉS 128 (2018), p.124; standing hypotheses on p.122)
items.note: Checked against the KP18 text. Its hypotheses are stronger than those printed in Cor. 1.3.18 (E27). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Frobenius of an abelian variety over a finite field is semisimple (cited)
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over F_q, the q-Frobenius π_A generates a commutative semisimple subalgebra Q[π_A] (a product of number fields) of End_Q(A); in particular π_A and its powers act semisimply on V_ℓ(A) (ℓ ≠ p) and on the Dieudonné isocrystal.
items.locator: §2.1.5, p.22 ('γ_{m,s0} induces a semi-simple automorphism'); §2.1.7, p.23 ('semisimplicity of γ_{m,s0}')
items.note: Weil/Tate. Also follows from P15 applied over F_q, since π_A is central in End_Q(A_{F_q}). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Comparison maps i_ℓ (ℓ ≠ p) and i_p
items.statement: The action of I_s0 on V̂^p(A_s0) gives a canonical map of A_f^p-groups A_f^p ⊗ I_s0 → I_{A_f^p,s0}; for ℓ ≠ p its ℓ-component i_ℓ: Q_ℓ ⊗ I_s0 → I_ℓ,s0 is injective. For ℓ = p, the action of I_s0 on D_{m,s0}, transported by (2.1.7.1), gives a canonical injection i_p: I_s0 ⊗_Q Q_p ↪ I_{p,s0} = I_{m,δ_s0} (m sufficiently divisible).
items.note: T09 and T16 presuppose these maps, but no item constructs them or states injectivity. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Existence of an auxiliary split prime ℓ0
items.statement: There exist primes ℓ0 ≠ p (infinitely many) such that G_{Q_ℓ0} is split and the characteristic polynomial of γ_{m,ℓ0,s0} splits over Q_ℓ0.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.1.9, p.24 ('Choose ℓ0 ≠ p a prime satisfying the conditions of Proposition 2.1.6')
items.note: By Chebotarev: take ℓ0 totally split in a number field that splits G and contains the roots of the characteristic polynomial of γ_{m,s0} ∈ End_Q(A_s0) on V_ℓ. That polynomial has rational coefficients independent of ℓ. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Rationality of the crystalline tensors at an F_q-point
items.statement: If the image of s0 in 𝒮_K(F̄_p) is defined over F_q, then for every m the tensors s_α,cris,s0 lie in D_{m,s0}^⊗, where D_{m,s0} is the descent of D_s0 to Q_{q^m} = W(F_{q^m})[1/p]. Hence the linear crystalline Frobenius γ_{m,cris,s0} = φ^{rm} (q = p^r) fixes them.
items.note: Asserted with only 'as these are φ-invariant' as justification, which does not suffice (E28). Follows from the canonicity in Prop. 1.3.7 by transport of structure. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Aut'(H) and conjugacy of maps defined over different extensions
items.statement: Let C and H be reductive algebraic groups over a field F of characteristic 0. Aut'(H) denotes the preimage of Out'(H) (2.1.8) in the group scheme Aut H of automorphisms of H. Two maps i_1, i_2: C → H, defined over extensions F_1, F_2 of F respectively, are conjugate (resp. conjugate by an element of Aut'(H)) if there are an extension F_3/F containing F_1 and F_2 and g ∈ H(F_3) (resp. g ∈ Aut'(H)(F_3)) with i_2 = g i_1 g^{-1} (resp. i_2 = g(i_1) := g ∘ i_1).
items.note: Used in the statements of Proposition 2.2.13 and Corollary 2.2.14 (items T24, T25). 'Preimage' presupposes the implicit embedding of Out'(H) into Aut H/H^ad; the embeddings F_1, F_2 ⊂ F_3 are part of the data (in the application all fields lie in one algebraically closed k). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Conjugating maximal tori while fixing a common element (the 'observation' in the proof of Proposition 2.2.13)
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0. (a) If T_1, T_2 ⊂ G are maximal tori and γ ∈ T_1(k) ∩ T_2(k), there is g ∈ G(k) with gT_1g^{-1} = T_2 and gγg^{-1} = γ. Indeed both T_i lie in the identity component M of the centralizer of γ, where they are conjugate. (b) If γ_1 ∈ T_1(k), γ_2 ∈ T_2(k) and σ(γ_1) = γ_2 for some σ ∈ Aut'(G)(k), then some σ' ∈ Aut'(G)(k) takes γ_1 to γ_2 and T_1 to T_2 (apply (a) to γ_2 ∈ σ(T_1) ∩ T_2).
items.note: Unnumbered, and used three times later in the same proof (p.30): with I_0 in place of G, and with T_1 = T_2 = T_0. The paper's aside 'M is a Levi subgroup of G' is false for general γ (E36) but is not needed. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Weil's Riemann hypothesis: Frobenius is a p-Weil point
items.statement: Let s0 be defined over F_q, q = p^r. For every m ≥ 1 the Frobenius γ_{m,s0} ∈ I_{s0}(Q) is a p-Weil point. Its eigenvalues are algebraic integers that are units at all finite places not above p and have all complex absolute values q^{m/2}, so they are p-Weil numbers of weight rm.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.2.13, p.29 ('By the Weil conjecture for abelian varieties, γ_{m,s0} ∈ I(Q) is a Weil point')
items.note: Black box (Weil). Needed so that Proposition 2.2.2 applies to γ_{m,s0}. Planned: DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.1 plans Weil's estimate for curves and abelian varieties over finite fields.

items.name: Galois-stable conjugacy class of embeddings into a quasi-split group contains a rational one ([Kot82, Cor. 2.2])
items.statement: As used: let G* be a quasi-split connected reductive group over Q, T a Q-torus and ī: T_{Q̄} ↪ G*_{Q̄} an embedding as a maximal torus whose G*(Q̄)-conjugacy class is stable under Gal(Q̄/Q). Then this conjugacy class contains an embedding i^{T*}: T ↪ G* defined over Q.
items.note: Black box from Kottwitz, 'Rational conjugacy classes in reductive groups' (1982). Its exact hypotheses were not checked here. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Transfer of a maximal torus of the quasi-split inner form to G (local and global)
items.statement: Let G* be the quasi-split inner form of G with inner twisting ψ: G_{Q̄} ≃ G*_{Q̄}, and T ⊂ G* a maximal torus over Q. For F = Q or Q_v, T transfers to G over F if there is an F-embedding j: T_F ↪ G_F such that ψ ∘ j is G*(F̄)-conjugate to the inclusion T ⊂ G*. The embedding i^T: T ↪ G of Corollary 2.2.14 is such a transfer over Q.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.2.14, p.30 (used without definition; the local analogue for J_b is §1.1.16, item N30)
items.note: The global notion is used ('T transfers to G at every prime …', 'Hence T transfers to G by [LR87, Lem. 5.6]', 'writing i^T for the transfer') but is not defined in the paper. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Local transfer of T at all places (Corollary 2.2.14)
items.statement: In the setting of Corollary 2.2.14, with T ⊂ G* via the Q-embedding i^{T*}: T transfers to G_{Q_ℓ} for ℓ ≠ p, ∞, via i_ℓ|_T, which is defined over Q_ℓ. It transfers to G_{Q_p} because G is quasi-split at p, so the inner twisting is trivial at p. It transfers to G_R because the image of T in G^ad is anisotropic over R, T(R) being compact modulo the scalars.
items.note: The case at ∞ rests on the standard fact that an elliptic maximal torus transfers to any inner form having an elliptic maximal torus (G_R has one, from the Shimura datum). The paper does not spell this out. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: An open subgroup containing decomposition groups at almost all primes is everything (Chebotarev and Jordan)
items.statement: If an open subgroup H ⊂ Gal(Q̄/Q) contains, for every prime ℓ ≠ p, a decomposition group at ℓ (for some place of Q̄ over ℓ), then H meets every conjugacy class of Gal(Q̄/Q) (Chebotarev), and hence H = Gal(Q̄/Q) (Jordan's lemma in a finite quotient).
items.note: Black box. The paper cites 'Cebotarev density' for the first half and leaves Jordan's lemma implicit ('This implies that the conjugacy class of ī^T is invariant by Gal(Q̄/Q)'). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Existence of an accommodating embedding with the same adjoint datum ([Del79b, 2.3.10], [Noo06, 2.12])
items.statement: As used: given (G,X) of Hodge type, there are a symplectic Q-space (V',ψ') and an accommodating embedding ι': (G',X') ↪ (G_{V'}, H_{V'}), together with a map G'^der → G^der inducing an isomorphism of adjoint Shimura data (G'^ad, X'^ad) ≃ (G^ad, X^ad).
items.note: Black box. Input to the auxiliary construction T22. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Passage from γ^n to γ for neat γ ([Noo09, Prop. 3.2])
items.statement: As used: for a neat Weil point γ ∈ I_{s0}(Q) and n ≥ 1, if the image of i_ℓ(γ^n) in Conj'(G) is a Q-point independent of ℓ, then so is the image of i_ℓ(γ).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.2.2 (§2.2.7), p.28 ('the result then follows from γ^n, and γ by [Noo09, Prop. 3.2]')
items.note: Black box; the content is inferred from its use. It is also what justifies each later 'replacing γ'' by a power'. Noot's exact statement was not available here. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion
items.statement: An abelian variety over a finite extension of Q_p has good reduction if and only if, for some (equivalently every) ℓ ≠ p, its ℓ-adic Tate module is unramified. It is used, as in [Noo09, p.68], to show that A_{s''} has good reduction.
items.note: Black box (Serre–Tate). Planned: NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.5 plans the Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion.

items.name: ℓ-independence of characteristic polynomials of quasi-endomorphisms
items.statement: For γ ∈ End(A_{s0}) ⊗ Q, the characteristic polynomial of γ on V_ℓ(A_{s0}), ℓ ≠ p, has rational coefficients and does not depend on ℓ.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2.5, p.25 ('standard and follows from the Lefschetz trace formula')
items.note: Black box; it gives the first assertion of Lemma 2.2.5 (T17). Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Real approximation for G^ad
items.statement: G^ad(Q) is dense in G^ad(R). Hence, after conjugating G'^der → G^der by an element of G^ad(Q), the image of X' in X^ad contains h_0^ad.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.2.2 (§2.2.7), p.27; also invoked in the proof of Lemma 2.2.8, p.28
items.note: Black box. Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 plans weak approximation in the cases the group theorems justify.

items.name: Existence of special points
items.statement: Every Shimura datum (G,X) has a special point: a maximal Q-torus T ⊂ G and h_T ∈ X that factors through T_R.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.2.8, p.28 ('Consider a special point on Sh_K(G,X), corresponding to a pair (T, h_T)')
items.note: Used without citation (Deligne). Planned: ShimuraVarieties V4 plans the density, and so the existence, of special points.

items.name: Elements of I_{s0}(Q) are semisimple; maximal tori of I_{s0} satisfy the Serre condition
items.statement: Every γ ∈ I_{s0}(Q) is semisimple, so it lies in some maximal torus T ⊂ I_{s0} defined over Q. Every maximal torus T ⊂ I_{s0} satisfies the Serre condition, because its maximal R-split subtorus is contained in the subtorus G_m ⊂ I_{s0} of scalars (2.1.3).
items.note: Unnumbered, and used later: in the proof of Proposition 2.2.13 (p.30), where Lemma 2.2.10 is applied to a maximal torus of I, and for I_{s0''} in §2.2.7 (p.28). Semisimplicity follows from the compactness of I_{s0}(R) modulo scalars (2.1.3), and connectedness of I_{s0} is Corollary 2.1.9. The paper says the maximal R-split torus is 'either trivial, or' G_m; since the scalars lie in every maximal torus, it is always G_m. This is harmless. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Automorphisms agreeing on a maximal torus differ by an element of the torus
items.statement: If σ and g are automorphisms of a connected reductive group I_0 over an algebraically closed field k that agree on a maximal torus T_0, then g = σ ∘ Int(t) for some t ∈ T_0(k).
items.note: Standard structure theory, used without citation. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Comparison with Noot's notion of accommodating abelian varieties
items.statement: The embedding ι is accommodating (in the sense of §2.2.6) if and only if, for some (equivalently any) y ∈ Sh_K(G,X)(C) whose abelian variety A_y has Mumford–Tate group G, A_y is accommodating in the sense of Noot [Noo09, 2.3].
items.note: Asserted without proof. It is what lets [Noo09, Thm. 2.4] and [Noo09, §3] be quoted in §2.2.7. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: ℓ-adic and crystalline isogeny schemes and realization maps
items.statement: Let s0, s0' ∈ S_{K_p}(F̄_p) be defined over F_q. For ℓ ≠ p, Isog_ℓ(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) is the Q_ℓ-scheme assigning to a Q_ℓ-algebra R the set of R-linear isomorphisms R⊗_{Q_ℓ}V_ℓ(A_{s0}) → R⊗_{Q_ℓ}V_ℓ(A_{s0'}) that carry 1⊗γ_{m,ℓ,s0} to 1⊗γ_{m,ℓ,s0'} for all m sufficiently divisible. Isog(D_{s0},D_{s0'}) is the Q_p-scheme assigning to a Q_p-algebra R the set of 1⊗φ-equivariant R⊗L-linear isomorphisms R⊗_{Q_p}D_{s0'} → R⊗_{Q_p}D_{s0} that carry D_{m,s0'} to D_{m,s0} for m sufficiently large. Realization gives natural maps i_ℓ(s0,s0'): Q_ℓ⊗Isog(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) → Isog_ℓ(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) for ℓ ≠ p, and i_p(s0,s0'): Q_p⊗Isog(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) → Isog(D_{s0},D_{s0'}).
items.note: T27 states that these maps are isomorphisms (Tate), but no item defines their targets. The crystalline map runs D_{s0'} → D_{s0} (contravariant Dieudonné theory). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Non-emptiness of P_ℓ via conjugacy of Frobenius
items.statement: For every ℓ, including ℓ = p, and m sufficiently divisible: P_ℓ(s0,s0') is non-empty if and only if γ_{m,ℓ,s0} and γ_{m,ℓ,s0'} are conjugate in G(Q̄_ℓ); for ℓ = p these are γ_{m,p,s0}, γ_{m,p,s0'} ∈ G(Q_{q^m}). When non-empty, P_ℓ(s0,s0') is an I_{ℓ,s0}-torsor. The same holds for the analogue P_{ℓ,1} defined with any other collection of Hodge cycles defining G.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.3.5, p. 31 ('each scheme is non-empty if and only if … (even for ℓ = p)'); used in the proof of Proposition 2.3.11, p. 34
items.note: Asserted without proof. For ℓ = p it needs the fact that σ-conjugacy over Q̄_p⊗Q_{q^m} ≅ ∏Q̄_p (σ permuting the factors cyclically) is detected by the norm γ_{m,p} = δσ(δ)⋯σ^{rm-1}(δ). It is used outside the lemma, so it deserves its own node. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: A non-empty P satisfies the comparison of Conjecture 2.3.4
items.statement: If P(s0,s0') is non-empty, then for every ℓ, including p, the map P(s0,s0')⊗Q_ℓ → P_ℓ(s0,s0') induced by i_ℓ is an isomorphism. It is a closed immersion (via T27) equivariant for I_{s0}⊗Q_ℓ ≅ I_{ℓ,s0} (Corollary 2.1.9) between torsors under the same group.
items.locator: Implicit in the proof of Lemma 2.3.13, p. 34 ('Hence by Tate's theorem P^T := P^T(s0,s0') is non-empty')
items.note: This is the step that turns non-emptiness of P_ℓ^T into non-emptiness of P^T without assuming Conjecture 2.3.4. The paper cites only 'Tate's theorem'. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Torus action at the reduction of a special point
items.statement: Let T ⊂ G be a maximal torus and x ∈ X with h_x factoring through T_R. Let s0 ∈ S_{K_p}(F̄_p), defined over F_q, be the reduction of a Q̄_p-valued point s of Sh_{K_{T,p}}(h_x), K_{T,p} = K_p ∩ T(Q_p). Since T contains the Mumford–Tate group of A_s (for some Q̄_p ↪ C), there are natural embeddings T ↪ Aut_Q(A_s) ↪ Aut_Q(A_{s0}), and they exhibit T as a subtorus of I_{s0}.
items.note: This is the T-action on A_{s0'} used in Proposition 2.3.11, in Lemma 2.3.13 (definition of P^T) and in the definition of a CM lift. The torus is maximal in I_{s0}, since rank I_{s0} = rank G by Corollary 2.1.9 (the paper says only 'subtorus'). The action depends on the embedding j: T ↪ G, and twisting j by a rational Weyl element changes it. This is the source of the Lemma 2.3.13 counterexample. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: The constructed CM lift has the same Frobenius
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.3.11, the Q̄-isogeny CM lift (i,x,s0') constructed in its proof satisfies γ_{m,s0} = γ_{m,s0'} in T(Q) for m sufficiently divisible, where T acts on A_{s0'} through i (§2.3.9).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 2.3.11, p. 34 ('We claim that for m sufficiently divisible, γ_{m,s0} = γ_{m,s0'} ∈ T(Q)')
items.note: This is needed for Lemma 2.3.13, and hence for Corollary 2.3.14, but the statement of Proposition 2.3.11 does not record it. See E41 on Lemma 2.3.13. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Local Galois cohomology via the Kottwitz map (cited)
items.statement: For any connected reductive group H over Q_p: H^1(Q_p,H) ≅ H^1(Gal(Q_p^ur/Q_p),H(Q_p^ur)) ≅ (π_1(H)_{Γ_p})_tors. The first isomorphism comes from Steinberg's theorem; the second sends a cocycle c to κ_H(c_σ), σ the Frobenius.
items.note: Black box. With Lemma 1.3.9 (κ_G(δ_{s0}) = κ_G(δ_{s0'})) it gives triviality of P^T in H^1(Q_p,G). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Polarized isogeny torsor is trivial over R (cited)
items.statement: Let I'_{s0} ⊂ Aut_Q(A_{s0}) be the group of automorphisms respecting the polarization up to a scalar, and let P ⊂ Isog(A_{s0},A_{s0'}) be the subscheme of isogenies respecting polarizations up to a scalar; P is an I'_{s0}-torsor when non-empty. Then the class of P in H^1(R,I'_{s0}) is trivial.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.3.13, p. 35, citing [Kot92, Lem. 17.1]
items.note: Black box. The notation P clashes with P(s0,s0'), and 'Q^×-scalar' should be R^×-scalar on R-points. Missing: routed to route 5.

items.name: Triviality over R passes to the T-reduction (cited)
items.statement: For T ⊂ I_{s0} a maximal torus and P^T ⊂ P a T-reduction of the I'_{s0}-torsor P, triviality of the class of P in H^1(R,I'_{s0}) implies that the class of P^T in H^1(R,T) is trivial.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.3.13, p. 35, citing [Kis17, Lem. 4.4.5]
items.note: Black box, as used. Corollary 2.3.14 uses its conclusion (H^1(R,T), not only H^1(R,G)). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Twisting a CM lift by a rational point of G/T (cited)
items.statement: Let (j,x,s0') be a Q̄-isogeny CM lift of s0 with respect to T whose torsor P^T has trivial class in H^1(Q,G), represented by ω (so j' = ω^{-1}jω is defined over Q), with trivial image of ω in H^1(R,T). Then ω^{-1}h_xω = h_{x'} for some x' ∈ X, factoring through j'(T_R) [Kis17, 4.2.2]. If s0'' ∈ S_{K_p}(F̄_p) admits a lift to Sh_{K_{T,p}}(h_{x'}), then P(s0,s0'') is a trivial I_{s0}-torsor [Kis17, Prop. 4.2.6]. Hence (j',x',s0'') is an isogeny CM lift.
items.note: Black boxes from [Kis17], which works with hyperspecial level and p > 2; the paper does not discuss their use at general level K_p. The printed 'h_x' is corrected to 'h_{x'}' (E46). The printed '(G/T)(Q)' matches j' = ω^{-1}jω only with the coset convention σ(ω)ω^{-1} ∈ T (see notes). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Sections on a formally smooth lift give a convergent morphism (cited)
items.statement: If Y_R^h (the lift Y_R with the horizontal log structure t_{e+1}⋯t_r) is formally smooth over W and s_0 ∈ E^log(Y_n^h)^⊗ is a compatible system of sections for all n ≥ 1, then these sections define a morphism of convergent F-isocrystals s_0: 1 → E^{log⊗} over Spec A.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition A.6, p. 39, citing [Ogu84, Thm 2.11] ('as in')
items.note: Black box, applied to log structures by analogy. None of A11–A14 records it. Missing: routed to route 4.

routes.reason: BG0 already owns B(G), sigma-centralizers and inner Levis, and BG1 owns kappa, Newton classes and their order. Add KMPS local specialness, minuscule Levi and torus-transfer source lemmas here. Reuse existing root and torus declarations; do not create another roadmap for B(G). The false normalizer display and general inner-form transfer are required source gates. The ordinary-class adapter and explicit quaternion obstruction refine the existing inner-twist, invariant and basic-division-algebra tests; no competing B(G) owner is created.

routes.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: global tori and cohomological transfer
routes.reason: The upstream roadmap builds algebraic group structure and root data; the existing ReductiveGroupsPartII covers local topology, buildings, parahorics and the dual group. Neither states this global torus-transfer, H1-obstruction and Weil-point chain. Keep this arithmetic continuation distinct from the existing local continuation.
routes.brief: Extend Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), importing its group, torus, root-data and representation APIs. Import local fixers from Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII), finite adelic torus class number from Adelic algebraic groups (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3), and local Newton/tori inputs from Reductive bundles, B(G) and Newton strata (BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0–BG1). Prove that ker(H1(Q,T) to H1(Q_p,T)) surjects onto H1(R,T), finite-place approximation for maximal tori, the required local and global transfer statements, and the simply connected/abelianized H1 reduction used for rational CM lifts. Construct Serre-condition tori, prime-units, Weil points, neat cyclic closures, Conj and the specified type-D quotient Conj prime. Prove density of neat prime-Weil points for a split auxiliary prime and the corrected reduced separated dense-point automorphism lemma. General finite-field Hom and Rosati theory are imported, not rebuilt. Preserve G-global and G-noot as exact original-proof acquisition tasks; do not assert a Hasse principle for every torus. Corrections the design must carry: Lemma 2.2.11 needs S reduced and separated (E6); in the proof of Proposition 2.2.13 the centralizer M is not in general a Levi subgroup, though T_1 and T_2 are still conjugate in M(k) (E36); and in the proof of Proposition 1.2.5 the torus T′ ⊂ J_b must be chosen elliptic when G_{Q_p} is not quasi-split, so that it transfers (E20).

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: reduction and Honda–Tate theory
routes.reason: ShimuraVarieties V4–V8 constructs generic canonical models and CM theory, and PELModuli owns PEL integral moduli. The arbitrary allowed-prime Hodge-type normal model, tensor groups and all-maximal-torus CM lifts go beyond those scopes. The fixed split unitary good-prime Igusa application does not supply the general theorem.
routes.brief: Build on Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties V4–V8), Shimura data (ShimuraData D3–D5), Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli M1–M4), Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli), AutomorphicBundles B1, finite-flat Dieudonne theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2), and PadicHodgeTheory R06.5. Import BunGAndNewtonStrata local theory, ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII global transfer, and CrystallineCohomologyConvergentPartII coefficient descent. Normalize the closure of the Hodge-type generic model at the lattice-stabilizer level. Construct lift-independent crystalline tensors, the family G-isocrystal and nonempty locally closed Newton strata for admissible classes satisfying (1.1.3.1); prove the lower Newton closure inclusion. State mu-ordinary nonemptiness with existence and rational-Newton witness, and density with local integrality. Prove the all-primes automorphism comparison, then independence of neat Weil conjugacy and rational maximal-torus transfer. For G quasi-split at p with no adjoint type-D factor, and explicitly assuming Conjecture 2.3.4 for all pairs, prove geometric coefficient-isogeny CM lifts for every point and every maximal torus of its isogeny group. Prove this unconditionally for PEL A/C. With G_der simply connected and ker1(Q,G_ab)=0 prove rational coefficient-isogeny CM lifts; specialize to C and A_n with n odd, retaining the separate odd-degree unitary argument. Preserve polarization similitudes, distinguish Qbar coefficient torsors from Q-points, and leave the disconnected type-D variant behind its exercise-proof gate. Do not generalize the motivic remarks to a proved abelian-type theorem. Import C02 from BG1: the ordinary class exists for quasi-split G_{Q_p} (the torus average), and can fail to exist for inner forms (E8). Keep geometric density conditional on its actual class and component hypotheses. Preserve N29 and T23 repairs from cc-fb70e5. Corrections the design must carry: the μ-ordinary class of §1.3.15 exists when G_{Q_p} is quasi-split and must otherwise be assumed (E8); Corollary 1.3.18 needs the hypotheses of [KP18, Cor. 0.3] (E27); in the proof of Proposition 1.3.10 the place v′ of E_T must be the one induced by ι_p (E24); the proof of Corollary 1.3.13 must work with the Tannakian group of 𝒟 inside G_{s0}, since the printed equivalence is false (E9); the rationality of the crystalline tensors over Q_{q^m} in §2.1.5 needs the uniqueness of Proposition 1.3.7, not only φ-invariance (E28); in §2.2.7 G″ must require equal similitude factors (E32) and γ″₁ must be made neat by a further power (E34); Lemma 2.2.8 must use G ×_{G^ab} T (E5); and Lemma 2.3.13 is false as stated: the CM lift must also have the Frobenius of s0, as the lift built in Proposition 2.3.11 does, and Corollaries 2.3.14 and 2.3.15 must start from that lift (E41).

routes.title: Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations, Part II: convergent coefficient descent
routes.reason: CR.1 and CR.5 own crystalline/log foundations; CR.7 explicitly requires separate extensions for singular or nonproper coefficient settings. Appendix A supplies exactly such an extension. RD.3 overconvergent objects and RD.5 rigid-cohomological descent are different contracts, so neither is silently substituted.
routes.brief: Extend Crystalline cohomology, de Rham–Witt and logarithmic foundations (CrystallineCohomology), importing CR.1, CR.5 and the coefficient interface CR.7. Reuse Witt vectors and DividedPowers, finite-flat Dieudonne modules (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2), semistable abelian models (NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.3), and the precise comparison supplier of PadicHodgeTheory. Define log enlargements, convergent log F-isocrystals, log Dieudonne crystals and their rationalization. Prove the reduced-enlargement and p-adically closed-ideal comparisons. For flat normal finite-type S/W, a relative Cartier boundary D, U=S minus D and an abelian scheme on U extending semi-abelianly to S, prove the Appendix A tensor-section extension: a global etale tensor section induces a unique convergent crystalline tensor section matching all permitted integral-point crystalline evaluations. Cover the proper semistable case first using the Eisenstein PD enlargement system, then the general case through alterations, proper descent and pointwise faithfulness. Keep horizontal and vertical log structures distinct. Import existing generic alterations/descent suppliers wherever exact contracts exist; specialize them here rather than re-planning their foundations. Close G-crystal before claiming the singular-base tensor construction complete. Correction the design must carry: the reduction step in the proof of Corollary A.7 must also make the abelian scheme extend semi-abelianly over the alterations S_i, for example by altering a compactification over which it already extends (E49).

routes.reason: A6 owns finite-dimensional rational Hom/End and Rosati positivity. Its reusable API should include the unit group, rational coefficient Isom open locus, real polarization-isometry compactness, and the unpolarized endomorphism-compatible rational-point argument. These are generic suppliers used by KMPS, not Shimura-specific definitions.

The current PAPER-SMITH-24 extraction already routes finite-field Honda–Tate to the Tate-isogeny layer R28.4. Its existing README supplies the generic rational Hom comparison and keeps the Hom-side algebra in AbelianSchemes A6. Add this finite-field source contract there, explicitly separating it from the number-field proof; no duplicate finite-field Part II is proposed. This routing does not claim the current number-field roadmap proves the finite-field or crystalline theorem.
routes.contract: For abelian varieties over a finite field, prove Hom⊗Q_ell equals Frobenius-equivariant rational Tate-module Hom for ell≠p and the contravariant crystalline analogue for ell=p. Treat sufficiently divisible finite extension for geometric Hom, functorial composition, duality and invertible loci. Import Hom/End from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6 and Dieudonne realization from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2. Close G-tate with Tate66 and the original crystalline source.
